quest.title: A Knight's Merit
quest.description: The Knights are busy preparing for an award ceremony in front of the Favonius Cathedral plaza...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x650, Mora x49200, Hero's Wit x6, Mystic Enhancement Ore x11

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? It's not a holiday or anything, is it? Why's it so lively in here?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: ...Prepare a few more strings of colored flags. As for the celebratory wine... I'll do the quality check in person.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: This is our first award ceremony since the expeditionary force's triumphant return. We're looking to put on a show, you hear?

dialogues.speaker: Raymond
dialogues.text: Leave it to us, Captain Kaeya!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: An award ceremony?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Oh? The Honorary Knight and Paimon? Well, this saves me the trouble of sending someone to invite you.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: I'm sure our colleagues from the expedition will be delighted to see such prestigious guests in attendance.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Knights are giving out awards?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Well, I'm sure you know how many Knights bear unique titles, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Take the Grand Master's "Boreas" or Captain Eula's "Spindrift," for example... Some they inherit. Others have unique origins...

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: But in the vast majority of cases, they are titles conferred to honor said knight's conduct and achievements.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Like how I'm the "Honorary" Knight?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Hmm... You could say that! Shame we were so busy with the issue of Dvalin's corruption back then, or we'd have held a ceremony for you, too... Let me think. Why don't we make it up to you this time?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's fine, it's been so long, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Besides, isn't this ceremony meant for the knights who're back from the expedition in triumph? We wouldn't want to steal their thunder!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Plus, being honored guests is way more impressive than actually receiving a title! Y'know, makes us sound like big shots!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You might actually have a point there...

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Is that so? In that case, I'm looking forward to seeing you at the ceremony.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: By the way, who's getting titles this time around?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Mostly those who've made outstanding contributions during the expedition: Winfried, Leifhelm...

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: And Lohen, Vice Captain of the 5th Company.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait. Him? You mean he doesn't have one yet?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: If it were just a question of personal ability, he'd have received a title before the expedition even started.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: But he hasn't been with us for very long, and... Well, let's just say there are personal reasons for the delay.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Word is that he'll not only gain a title, but also official command over 5th Company.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Why, by my count, he's even set to break a certain someone's record.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: "The youngest Captain of the Knights of Favonius," of course... The previous record holder was our former Cavalry Captain, Diluc.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Hehe. I wonder what face our "former Captain" will make when that happens.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm guessing he won't make any face.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Ah, ah, I wouldn't be so sure. He smiled oh-so-brilliantly the day he set that record...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A smiling champion of justice, huh...? Yeah, nah, Paimon can't see it...

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Well, let's not dwell on that. Care to guess what title our dear Vice-Captain Lohen will receive?

choices.text: Oh, we're playing name games, are we?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Gotcha, easy! So, Lohen... Lohen... "Dagger Knight"? "Smirking Knight"? Uh... Right! "Punching Bag Knight"!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Your skills are fading, Paimon...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nuh-uh! This guy's just... hard to sum up! Anyway. What's his title gonna be?

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Hmm, I'd say most signs right now point to...

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: —"The Benevolent Knight."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Benevolent?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How's that even slightly associated with him!?

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Haha... Long story. Alas, it seems someone has come looking for you.

response.speaker: Porthos
response.text: Honorary Knight! Honorary Knight! Thank goodness, you're actually here.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Is there something you need from me?

response.speaker: Porthos
response.text: Uhm... The Grand Master would like you to come to the Knights of Favonius Headquarters. He says he has important matters to discuss!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Varka? What important business would he have with us?

choices.text: Looking for an excuse to slack off, maybe...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon can't say she'd be surprised... But it's not like he's never serious, so maybe something really has come up...

choices.text: Let's go see him, just in case...

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: See you later — remember to attend the ceremony!

choices.text: Maybe he wants to sneak out for a drink...

talks.objective: Go to the Knights of Favonius Headquarters

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...Any questions about the award ceremony arrangements? Perhaps... Are you even listening?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm, okay. No objections.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...*cough* Lohen!

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Huh... Yeah. Can I go now? Thanks a lot, Grand Master!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: —Hey! Get back here!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: *sigh*... What is it with you young people these days? When I first earned my title, I was so excited I couldn't sleep a wink all night...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Huh? Oh? And how many barrels of wine did you guzzle while counting sheep?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...That's not the point!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: *sigh*... Forget it. I know you're not interested in a knightly title — or the position of Captain.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: But it's Adorno's final wish to have you inherit the title of Benevolent Knight before he officially retires.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: You've been back in Mondstadt for a while now, and you're usually stationed at Dornman Port... Have you not thought about going to see him?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: ...Hey, there have been too many reports to file since our return from the expedition. I haven't been able to find the time.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Oh? Odd that the handwriting on the reports you've submitted looks rather like Gunther's, wouldn't you say?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Ugh... Can't even handle a little "paperwork"... He still needs more training.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Anyway — go have a good talk with Adorno. We'd like a smooth transition for both the title and the position of Captain.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Consider this a direct order from yours truly, the Grand Master, so don't go using work as an excuse, you hear?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Eh, don't look so worried. I've a rough idea of the agreement you two made before the expedition. If you need someone to cover for you...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...I mean, considering Adorno's special circumstances, I can make an exception and go with you.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: ...Uh, forget it. You two've worked together for so long, he'd see right through you with a glance.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: *sigh* True... And besides, I've got other matters to attend to... Is there anyone else you can take?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Someone convincing, but not too close to Adorno... Do we have such a knight here in Mondstadt?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Hah, that "knight" you speak of... has just arrived.

choices.text: So, is that why you borrowed Varka's name...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: I was troubled, troubled, I tell you, but then I just happened to see you two walking by from the window. This must be the Anemo Archon's guidance, don't you think?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Not at all! Paimon's not sure what's going on yet, but you just want us to help you scam someone, don't you?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Oh no, no, no, no, no, not at all! Honesty is a knight's badge of virtue. I'd just like you to "play the part" of my "friends."

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: ...And corroborate some of the expedition's events while you're at it. Relax. If I say a single lie... feel free to punch me, alright?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait. There's a ton of problems with that! We didn't even meet up with Varka until the very end of the expedition, and we didn't run into you in Nod-Krai, either...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Ah, right. Speaking of "friends," I've heard tell of a certain "friendly custom"...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: —The "friendship fee." Here. I insist.

choices.text: What kind of custom is that!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Th—That's a lot of friendship!

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: I receive an allowance for special missions. Guess it all piled up before I knew it. I don't really have any use for so much money, so... why not give it to a friend?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Y'know... We could always do with another friend... don't you think?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What about those problems you mentioned!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: P—Problems are meant to be solved! F—For the sake of friends...!

choices.text: Setting aside whether we're doing this for a friend or a friendship fee...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: ...Adorno the Benevolent Knight. Captain of the 5th Company, and my direct superior.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Benevolent Knight... Wasn't that...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: The knightly title I'm about to inherit? It seems that's the rumor. But in truth, he and I made a pact...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: In return for recommending me for the expedition, he hoped I, in turn, would reflect on what it truly means to be a virtuous knight while I was away.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Once it was all over, I'd then inherit the title Benevolent Knight from him... as well as the position of Captain.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhm, wait, does that mean... You aren't confident you can get his approval, and that's why you want us to go along with your little show?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Don't get me wrong — I have no interest in titles or positions. I'd just... rather not listen to his nagging.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Did he not join the expedition himself?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Oh, he'd have loved to. He's a real veteran of Varka's campaigns. Wouldn't have missed that show for the world...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: ...If age and strength were still on his side. But I imagine it is now his final wish to find the "Benevolent" title a home.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is that so? Then we'll...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Got it. I'll tag along for the ride.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Haha! I knew that would do the trick. Off we go, then — to Dornman Port.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! How much of what you just said was true, huh? You sure you're not out to scam this Adorno guy?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: "The situation in Sumeru is as described above... It is time to eliminate the remaining poison Dottore has left in Mondstadt."

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: *sigh*... Eroch... Ursa... It's been a while since I last heard those names. I can feel a headache coming on...

choices.text: I'm starting to wonder who this Adorno is.
What kind of friend are you talking about!?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Hey, old man! Still kicking, I see?

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: Heh. Didn't buy the farm during the expedition? Thought you might've fallen into some pit somewhere, what with how long it's taken you to come see me.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Ah, you worry too much. When it comes to pits, I've been the one doing all the digging and burying.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...That's a novel way to say hello...

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: Who are these two?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: #My friend — the "Honorary Knight" — and {M#his}{F#her} guide, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: "Honorary Knight"... The same one that resolved the Stormterror incident...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: #Oh, {M#he}{F#she} didn't just resolve that incident — {M#he}{F#she} helped us complete the expedition. The Wild Hunt, The Doctor, Andrius... {M#He}{F#She} played a part in dealing with all of them.

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: Oh? I've quizzed the knights at Dornman Port about what happened during the expedition.

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: Unfortunately, for some reason, none of them were willing to tell me the whole story... It's almost as if someone told them to avoid me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Lohen... was that your doing?)

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: Since we've got a moment, let's have a proper chat. How did this magnificent knight here end up making friends with you?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Hmm, I suppose it's because we both possess a "chivalric spirit" that shines as bright as Mora. Isn't that right, Paimon?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah... Just like Mora, haha...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: I've been keeping my promise to you, you know. For instance...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: I've been organizing group training sessions with my fellow knights every week to build ironclad trust between "friends"...

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: Oh, right, the team building I told you about! Great way to foster trust and chemistry.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Hmm... As for this week's "training plan"...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Drugging the wine one night in advance...)

response.speaker: Leifhelm
response.text: Ugh... My stomach... My stomach!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Secretly swapping a teammate's ammo...)

response.speaker: Winfried
response.text: What sorcery is this!? Huh? What do you mean, "there are no bullets in your gun"...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Digging traps at the training grounds...)

response.speaker: Ekbert
response.text: Surely the Vice-Captain can't take us all out if we swarm him at once? C'mon, let's get him— Aaah!

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: *scoff* Real combat's ten times harder than training, and the enemy's a hundred times more cunning than I am.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Remember this well. Once you're on the battlefield, the only one you can truly "trust" is yourself!

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: And so, to ensure the absolute safety of my "friends," I went out every night, eliminating potential threats around our stronghold...

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: Hmm... Vigilance and reconnaissance are indeed things a Company Captain needs to pay attention to...

talks.objective: Serve as a witness for Lohen's expedition experiences

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Yes, yes. Quality control for our drinks... That'll require a personal touch.

talks.objective: Serve as a witness for Lohen's expedition experiences
Serve as a witness for Lohen's expedition experiences
Serve as a witness for Lohen's expedition experiences

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Hah... Just ensuring my "friends" get a good night's rest. All in a day's work, you know?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Of course, in order to gather intel for the expeditionary force, I also needed to maintain my "connections" at all times... and communicate earnestly with my friends...

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: Haha, I didn't expect you to have matured so much from one trip...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Come, let me sprinkle some more salt on the cut...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Perhaps another dash of pepper...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: A sprinkling of spices to finish things off...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Mmhmm, now THIS is how you grill meat!

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Here. Would you like some? I mean, you've had nothing for nearly three days. Or... would you like to try something else?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: ...Oh? May I take this to mean that we have an agreement?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: You'll cooperate? Lovely! That makes us "friends" from now on — and you know how it is between friends. No betrayals, you understand...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: See, you two? I didn't lie, did I?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You, uh... didn't... somehow...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: And that's the story, old man. Now pass on that Benevolent Knight title... thing, and get some well-deserved rest, alright?

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: Hey now, we aren't finished talking yet, are we? Word is that you faced a truly formidable foe while in Nod-Krai...

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: Someone called... the Rächer of Solnari, I believe?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, really!? Why haven't we heard you and Varka talk about that?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: ...Ha, there's nothing to tell...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: ...I was with the Grand Master when we ambushed Rerir. But not only was I useless, I even ended up acting as a punching bag.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: That left me laid up in camp for several days. By the time I could finally get out of bed, I heard the news... that you had all joined forces to banish him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, so that's why Paimon didn't see you when we were duking it out with Rerir... It's not like you to miss a fight...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Paimon...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! Sorry...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: No need to apologize. You're right. I wasn't strong enough...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: I was slow, weak, powerless... mortal.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Lohen! Lohen... Hey! You! Take him and fall back!

choices.text: He was a Sinner who once set his face against the world...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! In the end, we had to use his power against him just to banish him... So don't worry about it too much!

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: ...But he was once a mere mortal too, wasn't he?

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: Ahem. Well, I haven't seen this Rächer of Solnari with my own eyes, but I believe that strength alone does not a "knight" make.

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: Anyway, I've got some important work to attend to. You and your friends can come along if you'd like, Lohen.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Important work? Aren't you already semi-retired?

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: Hah, just follow me and you'll see. Consider this required reading for any "Benevolent Knight."

choices.text: He wields Abyssal powers far beyond our imagination.

talks.objective: Follow Adorno to finish his work

dialogues.speaker: Max
dialogues.text: Ah! The Benevolent Knight is here!

dialogues.speaker: Moricztill
dialogues.text: Grandpa Adorno!

dialogues.speaker: Northland Cat
dialogues.text: Meow~

dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: Hey now — no rushing, and no snatching! Easy now. Line up properly!

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: Eh, it's alright, it's alright. They're just kids. A little excitement is a good thing. Here you go. Today's candy.

dialogues.speaker: Moricztill
dialogues.text: Thanks, Grandpa!

dialogues.speaker: Max
dialogues.text: Ooh, this is great!

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: ...Is this the "important work" you spoke of?

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: Oh, we're just getting started, "recruit." Try to keep up!

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: ...Understood, Captain.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Ugh...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: I should be the one asking you — how are you so skilled at this?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: I can barely imagine our Honorary Knight doing things like this all day long...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We don't spend every waking hour fighting bad guys who wanna destroy the world, y'know... Also, the world would be a way scarier place if that happened every day!

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Daily routine, huh... I've been back in Mondstadt for a while now, but adapting... hasn't been easy.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Not long ago, camping in the wild and facing constant danger was our "daily routine."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But you were still on the expedition then, right? Now you can finally relax!

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: You think so? Personally, I find it hard to feel at ease with any sort of "daily routine."

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: It was the Anemo Archon who scattered the snowstorms that once swept Mondstadt, the Knights of Favonius who won the peace we now enjoy through conquest. A single unexpected incident could bring it all crashing down.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: So... rather than waiting for someone to turn my "daily routine" on its head, I find it more reassuring to follow an "extraordinary routine."

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: We Knights are needed precisely because the world is so fragile.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, are you done handing out the candy already?

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: Indeed. Looks like you're all wrapped up here as well. Thanks for exercising such patience.

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: This next task should give you a chance to stretch your legs. We're going to patrol the surrounding area for monsters.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Monsters? What, are the Knights shorthanded? You haven't held a sword in years.

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: Hey now, my retirement isn't official yet! It's just a patrol. I'm still more than capable of handling myself.

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: Things did get a bit tough a while back... but look at me now, eh? Might as well get going while I've still got pep in my step.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Never one to sit still, were you... Fine. Where are we headed?

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: We've had strange monsters show up around the outskirts. No one's gotten hurt yet, but you can never be too careful.

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: Usually, I just patrol the area for any approaching monsters, but this time, I've got you for backup.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Heh! Forget about just patrolling — we can take them all on, no problem! Right?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Piece of cake.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: ...Sure. Let's go.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? That's weird... Paimon thought he'd be more excited...

choices.text: Were you expecting a "Let me try my blade with you," or something?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, uh... Why not? *sigh* Paimon doesn't get him at all...

choices.text: But this is our actual daily routine.
Such is the life of an adventurer.
I've never seen you this exhausted, even after a fight.

talks.objective: Head to your destination and patrol

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Weird, no signs of anything unusual here... Are there really monsters nearby?
If you're looking for the ones that have been behaving strangely, I fear you're here too late.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: It seems someone beat the Knights of Favonius to the punch and took care of them already.

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: Diluc? What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: #Long time no see, Mr. Adorno. You too, {NICKNAME}, Paimon... Lohen.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhm... Were the monsters here wiped out by a certain Darknight Hero by any chance?

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: No.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you sure?

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: ...I'm not personally familiar with this "Darknight Hero" you speak of, but based on the rumors I've heard, the traces left on this battlefield don't match his style.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: This looks more like someone... obtained advance intel on the monsters and came to "clean up." Not even a single scrap remains.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Oh? So it would appear you're here to investigate, Master Diluc? That's odd. Why would the boss of the Dawn Winery be interested in monsters?

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Dawn Winery's caravans pass through Dornman Port. The rumors left me ill at ease, so I decided to see for myself.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: As for the Knights of Favonius... are they still understaffed even with the expedition's return?

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: Hah, strict as ever, I see. I took this patrol up myself — gotta keep moving while I still can.

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: I've been living this life for decades. Can't just sit idle, you know?

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: ...Thank you for your hard work, venerable Benevolent Knight.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Wait, what? Not even Varka gets that much respect from Diluc!

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Heh. I'd say that's Varka's problem.

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: *sigh* Eroch only got away with causing that uproar by taking advantage of the Grand Master's absence.

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: If he and the Alder Knight had been here, they never would have allowed Crepus's heroism in driving off the dragon to go unrecognized.

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: ...And we old codgers back in Mondstadt wouldn't have been the only ones left to stand up for your father.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: ...But they weren't there, were they?

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: #Let's cut the small talk. Since there are no clues here, I have no reason to stay. Goodbye, {NICKNAME}, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: And... take care, "Benevolent Knight."

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: *sigh* Ursa... Eroch... Even when gone, some foes leave wounds that won't easily heal.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Hmm? Need me to explain? Sure. Ursa was a wicked dragon who could really take a beating, and Eroch was an Inspector who could've really used one...

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: *cough* ...Allow me instead. Ursa the Drake was a dragon who first appeared in Mondstadt a thousand years ago, bringing calamity with its immense might.

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: After the Knights of Favonius were founded, our first Grand Master, Vennessa, sealed it away with the Anemo Archon's help. After that, the dragon sank into slumber...

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: However, just a decade ago, it appeared in Mondstadt once again!

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: With the Grand Master away, its timing could not have been worse. Not only that, it would lie low when the Knights of Favonius mobilized to attack, only to suddenly reemerge when they were resting...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Such perfect timing!?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: In the end, it was also "perfect timing" that the Fatui Harbinger who exterminated it just so happened to be "passing through."

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: That's right, your old friend — The Doctor. Or would it be more accurate to say one of his Segments?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, Ursa the Drake waking up... it was all part of some plot by that Segment?

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: Not entirely. Even a Fatui Harbinger would've struggled to stir up such a storm in Mondstadt all by themselves.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So, there was someone else pulling the strings?

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: Indeed. There was one other person who, seduced by transcendent power, secretly colluded with The Doctor...

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: He was the then-Inspector of the Knights of Favonius, and the greatest traitor to the Knights in a hundred years — Eroch.

choices.text: The former Inspector of the Knights...

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: ...When Diluc had just come of age, Ursa attacked a trade caravan from the Dawn Winery.

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: It should've been nothing more than a common raid, a tactic they commonly used to incite fear.

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: But the swaggering dragon was driven back by a mere merchant — Diluc's father, Crepus... who paid the ultimate price.

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: News of this defeat did not favor Eroch's plan to seize power through terror, so he suppressed the truth, claiming he was doing so to "maintain the honor of the Knights."

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: If only I had discovered a moment sooner that he and The Doctor were working hand in glove... perhaps I could have stopped everything that followed.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: That's not your burden to shoulder alone. Eroch hid his true colors well — up until the incident with Ursa.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: ...Even his victims had no idea who was responsible for their suffering.

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: *sigh*

choices.text: They may have got away with it for a time...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: ...We needn't continue to live in the shadows of scum like that, old man.

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: ...Hmm, you've got a point. We've got long lives ahead of us, after all.

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: Let's get on with our next task, eh? This should lift your spirits a bit, I'm sure — we'll be assisting the 10th Company with their research.

choices.text: But they've all paid the price for their sins now.
So what's his relationship with Diluc?

talks.objective: Go to assist in the experiment

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Hmm... It's as we thought — the magic Miss Alice left behind isn't so easily understood.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Sucrose... Huh? Is this...

choices.text: The bubble we used to welcome the expeditionary force?

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: #Ah, {NICKNAME}! Are you here to assist with the development tests for the Simulation Training Bubble: Type 02?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Is that... the magic bubble that can recreate memories?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You've used it too?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: I was told not long after my return that I could use this to catch up with the various events, large and small, that transpired during our absence.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: ...But using this level of magic for... well, storytelling seems like a huge waste of resources.

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: You're not alone in thinking that. Our Investigation Team quickly recognized its broader potential for training simulations.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: If we could recreate formidable enemies from senior knights' memories and incorporate them into realistic, safe training simulations, that could help raise the whole organization's combat prowess.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: However, we've been debugging the bubble for a while now, and we still haven't fully grasped its underlying principles... We're also struggling to balance realism with safety...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Safety"... doesn't sound like something Alice would give much thought to.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: That so? Sounds interesting. Let me give it a shot.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: You're not here to take part, are you, pops?

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: Oh, not to worry. I know exactly how much strength these old bones have left in them. I'm just here to provide the "memories" inside my head.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Oh? Then who was the tester in your original plan?

response.speaker: Theodore
response.text: Miss Sucrose, the test arrangements are... Ah... Lohen?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: ...Theodore?

response.speaker: Theodore
response.text: Why are you...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: I just happened to come along with Adorno to test this Simulation Training Bubble. I take it you're the scheduled tester?

response.speaker: Theodore
response.text: Ah... Yes, that's right. And these are...

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: #*cough* Let me introduce you. These two are the Honorary Knight and {M#his}{F#her} guide, Paimon.

response.speaker: Theodore
response.text: The Honorary Knight? I didn't expect someone so distinguished...

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: And this is Theodore, a trainee medic with the 8th Company. Like you, he's one of Lohen's friends.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Lohen? ...Friends?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: No need to sound so surprised. I have plenty of "friends," don't I, Paimon?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Y—Yeah...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Paimon wonders how much this guy's "friendship fee" was...)

response.speaker: Theodore
response.text: Hmm...?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Theodore, isn't rescue and medical care more your thing? How did you end up getting roped into testing?

response.speaker: Theodore
response.text: Uhm, I actually helped to construct this simulation, so I understand a few of its basic principles.

response.speaker: Theodore
response.text: Besides, I trained to become a knight, too. And even if something happens, I should be able to patch myself up...

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: But you needn't force yourself to do this if Vice-Captain Lohen's willing to take over. We might get more practical test data from frontline knights too, so...

response.speaker: Theodore
response.text: Y—Yeah, I suppose Lohen's the better pick...

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: Chin up, Theodore. If anything happens to Lohen, we'll be counting on you to treat him.

response.speaker: Theodore
response.text: ...Alright.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: I doubt there's a memory out there that can hurt me... but let's get started, old man.

choices.text: Looks like something the Hexenzirkel cooked up...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: No fluctuation in pain parameters... Hmm. Should we switch to a more... normal test subject?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: No need. Let's continue the test.

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: Are you sure? I don't think my memories will yield anything worth fighting against at this point...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Uh, don't we have a knight right here who's faced more terrifying foes?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Come on... Show me the Rächer of Solnari — as you remember him.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Are you sure?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: I'm not so disheartened that I'd fear his memory. I just wanna see...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: If I'm still as... powerless as he claimed.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: ...Urgh!

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: ...Wake up! Lohen!

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: ...*panting*...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Ah, Mr. Adorno! Are you...

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: I'm fine... Just threw my back out... Gotta take a break, that's all... But Lohen...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: *cough* Ungh...

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: Wound up hurting yourself from trying to hold back that final blow, didn't you...

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: Theodore, go get him checked over. Last thing we want is to miss a serious injury.

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: Alright... Lohen, come with me.

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: *cough*

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Mr. Adorno! Are you alright?!

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: It's no big deal... Just got old. Things stick with you once you're over the hill, waiting to be set off by the slightest exertion... *sigh* Guess I'll have to ask Theodore for another prescription.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is there... something up with Lohen?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Could there be a problem with the magic? But if there were issues with the reproduced memories, the Honorary Knight should have noticed...

choices.text: I tried to control the projection, too...

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: Are you saying the problem... lies with Lohen himself?

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: ...Did the battle with the Rächer of Solnari set him off again...

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: ...Lohen's pursuit of power began long ago.

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: The traitor, Eroch, collaborated with The Doctor on forbidden experiments in his quest for greater power...

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: Lohen nearly became one of their test subjects.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Experiments by The Doctor!?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Could he be just like Collei...)

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: Fortunately, the Knights tracked Eroch's cronies down, uncovering their plots before they could act.

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: They cut their experiments short and tried to transport their victims away... But we intercepted them in transit and rescued everyone.

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: ...It's alright. It's over now.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: I heard about that. That was the incident that saw you gain the title of "Benevolent Knight," right?

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: I'd never have guessed that Vice Captain Lohen was involved...

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: *sigh* I never deserved that title. We saved the kidnapped children, yes, but I failed to root Eroch out.

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: I couldn't find their experiment site. Nor could I help Lohen fully shake off the trauma of that incident.

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: He's always believed he needs power to stay free from others' control. I'd hoped the expedition might change his perspective, but...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that's what happened...

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: ...It's tough having to act the part of a "friend" with someone like him, huh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah... Wait!

choices.text: You saw right through us, didn't you?

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: Haha, I may be getting old, but my eyes haven't failed me yet.

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: Ignoring his methods, the fact that he's found companions willing to play along with his little charade shows he's made at least some progress.

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: Even if you're just acting, maybe learning from you will finally help him figure it out.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Hmm...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sucrose? What's wrong?

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: There's something I'm concerned about... Honorary Knight, would you mind taking a look at this?

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: ...Strange. Mr. Adorno said that Lohen's obsession may have caused the projection to spiral out of control.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: However, the Simulation Training Bubble: Type 02's parameters were all normal... If anything, it was the power Vice Captain Lohen released at that moment that appeared unusual.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you haven't seen anything like this before?

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: No... It's not the elemental energy we usually encounter, and it isn't the "Void Realm energy" that Mr. Albedo talks about either... Do you have any ideas what it might be, Honorary Knight?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (I thought I sensed... some familiar power back there... but I can't be certain.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you think there's something up with Lohen? He's not... messing about with something dangerous, is he?

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: That's not what I meant. I'm just reporting my findings. We shouldn't accuse our companions of anything untoward — not without evidence.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You have a point! We've just run into this sorta thing way too many times... Can't be too careful...

response.speaker: Theodore
response.text: Why did you come here today? We clearly agreed—

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Varka's orders. Not my decision.

response.speaker: Theodore
response.text: Even so, that was way too careless of you. Using so much power... *sigh*

response.speaker: Theodore
response.text: ...What if we're exposed?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Hehe, then... We'll just have to accelerate our experiments before that happens.

choices.text: I don't think the magic is the problem.
